question: The largest four-digit number which, when divided by 14, 9 and 6, leaves remainder 2 in each case is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required number − 2 must be divisible by 14, 9, 6

LCM(14, 9, 6) = 126

Largest multiple of 126 below 9999 = 126 × 79 = 9954

Add remainder: 9954 + 2 = 9956

**∴ Answer = 9956**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number leaves remainder 2 when divided by 14, 9 and 6

**Formula used:**

Number = LCM × k + remainder

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM(14, 9, 6) = 126

⇒ Let number = 126k + 2

⇒ Largest 4-digit number = 9999

⇒ 126k + 2 ≤ 9999 ⇒ 126k ≤ 9997

⇒ k = 79

⇒ Number = 126 × 79 + 2 = 9954 + 2 = 9956

**∴ The correct answer is 9956.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Concept

LCM gives the common multiple for divisibility conditions.

Remainder Rule

Subtract remainder to make number divisible.

General Form

Number = LCM × k + remainder

Maximum Value

Choose largest k within given limit.
